title: Simulation Task
description: Develop a multi-agent simulation system that models the spread of mask-wearing behavior through social networks.
simulation_focus: Predict agents' mask-wearing behavior over day 30 - day 39 (last ten days) based on their attributes, social connections, and past behavior
Model information propagation and behavioral changes triggered by social influence and government intervention starting on Day 10

data_files.agent_attributes.csv: Contains demographic and behavioral attributes of each agent, including age, occupation, risk perception, and social connection counts
data_files.social_network.json: Contains structured data representing a social network. Each entry corresponds to a user (identified by a unique integer ID), and the values describe the different types of relationships that user has with others. Data Structure: The top-level structure is a dictionary ({} in JSON). Keys: Each key is a unique user ID (as an integer, e.g., 0, 1, 2, etc.). Values: Each value is another dictionary with the following fields: "family": a list of user IDs representing family connections. "work_school": a list of user IDs representing colleagues or schoolmates. "community": a list of user IDs representing community-level acquaintances. "all": a merged list of all user IDs connected to the user across the three categories above.
data_files.train_data.csv: Time series data for the first 30 days, used for training the model

RMSE.description: Root Mean Square Error measuring overall predictive accuracy of mask adoption rates
RMSE.interpretation: Directly interpretable as percentage deviations due to the 0-1 range

interactions.name: peer_influence
interactions.description: Persons observe the mask status of their neighbors; if perceived support exceeds their threshold (or via a logistic decision rule), they adopt.

interactions.name: social_reinforcement
interactions.description: Repeated exposures from multiple neighbors increase the probability of adoption (complex contagion).

interactions.name: information_broadcast
interactions.description: Public health authority and media broadcast messages that shift risk perception and adoption propensity.

interactions.name: policy_mandate_enforcement
interactions.description: Mandates increase perceived benefits or costs of non-compliance; enforcement and penalties affect adoption and dropout.

interactions.name: tie_rewiring_homophily
interactions.description: People rewire social ties based on homophily in mask status or beliefs, affecting diffusion pathways.

interactions.name: location_based_contact
interactions.description: Contacts are modulated by shared locations (households, workplaces, etc.), altering exposure frequency.

metrics.name: adoption_rate_over_time
metrics.description: Proportion of agents wearing masks at each time step.

metrics.name: final_adoption_rate
metrics.description: Proportion of agents wearing masks at the end of the simulation.

metrics.name: time_to_50_percent_adoption
metrics.description: Number of steps until at least 50% of agents adopt mask-wearing.

metrics.name: cascade_size
metrics.description: Total number (or share) of adopters ultimately influenced by initial seeds.

metrics.name: behavior_reproduction_number_Rb
metrics.description: Average number of new adopters directly attributable to a single adopter within a short window.

metrics.name: adoption_churn_rate
metrics.description: Rate at which adopters drop the behavior per time step.

metrics.name: mean_exposures_before_adoption
metrics.description: Average number of neighbor exposures required before an agent adopts.

metrics.name: assortativity_by_adoption
metrics.description: Network assortativity coefficient based on mask adoption status.

metrics.name: inequality_of_adoption
metrics.description: Difference or Gini index of adoption rates across groups (e.g., age_group or group_id).

metrics.name: policy_effect_size
metrics.description: Change in adoption trend pre- vs post-mandate or campaign (e.g., difference-in-differences).

metrics.name: convergence_time
metrics.description: Number of steps until adoption rate change stays below a small threshold for a set lookback window.

metrics.name: peak_adoption_rate
metrics.description: Maximum observed adoption rate over the simulation period.
